spirit-cave-thailand.name: Spirit Cave
spirit-cave-thailand.summary: An archaeological site in northwestern Thailand occupied by prehistoric Hoabinhian hunter-gatherers between about 12,000 and 7,000 years ago.

hoabinhian.name: Hoabinhian
hoabinhian.summary: A stone-tool tradition linked to hunter-gatherer societies across Southeast Asia, dated from roughly 10,000 to 2000 BCE.

a-b-t-culture.name: Đa Bút culture
a-b-t-culture.summary: An early Neolithic period and site in Vietnam dated to about 5000 to 1000 BCE, excavated in the 1930s by Étienne Patte, showing evidence of hunting, fishing and early farming.

austroasiatic-languages.name: Austroasiatic languages
austroasiatic-languages.summary: A family of about 168 languages spoken across Mainland Southeast Asia, South Asia and southern China, including Vietnamese and Khmer, the only two used as national languages.

kra-dai-languages.name: Kra-Dai languages
kra-dai-languages.summary: Family of tonal languages spoken across mainland Southeast Asia, southern China and northeastern India, including Thai and Lao, with about 93 million speakers total.

chester-gorman.name: Chester Gorman
chester-gorman.summary: American archaeologist (1938–1981) who excavated Spirit Cave and other prehistoric sites in Thailand and discovered the site of Non Nok Tha.

steep-cliff-cave.name: Steep Cliff Cave
steep-cliff-cave.summary: An archaeological site in northwestern Thailand used by the Hoabinhian culture as a game jump in the early Holocene.

wilhelm-solheim.name: Wilhelm Solheim
wilhelm-solheim.summary: American anthropologist (1924–2014), a leading figure in Southeast Asian archaeology best known for his theory of an ancient maritime trading network across the Asia-Pacific region.

corbicula.name: Corbicula
corbicula.summary: A genus of freshwater clams originally native to East Asia, now invasive worldwide, with some species uniquely reproducing via androgenesis (all-male inheritance).

angono-binangonan-petroglyphs.name: Angono Petroglyphs
angono-binangonan-petroglyphs.summary: 127 carved human and animal figures on a rock wall between Angono and Binangonan in the Philippines, made before 2000 BC and considered the country's oldest known artwork.

b-c-s-n-culture.name: Bắc Sơn culture
b-c-s-n-culture.summary: A Neolithic period in Vietnam, a variant of the Hoabinhian tool tradition marked by a higher share of edge-ground cobble tools.

austronesian-peoples.name: Austronesian peoples
austronesian-peoples.summary: Peoples descended from a prehistoric seaborne migration out of Taiwan around 3000–1500 BCE, who used sails and outrigger boats to spread across the Indo-Pacific, from Madagascar to Easter Island and New Zealand.

h-a-b-nh-province.name: Hòa Bình
h-a-b-nh-province.summary: Former mountainous province in northwestern Vietnam, incorporated into Phú Thọ province in 2025, whose name gave rise to the archaeological term 'Hoabinhian'.

sumatralith.name: Sumatralith
sumatralith.summary: A unifacial stone tool of the Hoabinhian culture of Southeast Asian hunter-gatherers, made by flaking one side of a rounded pebble; it is a key marker for identifying Hoabinhian sites.

h-v-n-t-n.name: Hà Văn Tấn
h-v-n-t-n.summary: Vietnamese historian, archaeologist and scholar of Buddhism (1937–2019), born in Hà Tĩnh, who became a professor at Vietnam National University, Hanoi.

ng-m.name: Ngườm
ng-m.summary: Rock-shelter archaeological site in Thái Nguyên Province, northern Vietnam, excavated in 1981, with stone flakes radiocarbon-dated to about 23,000 years ago and an unusually high share of retouched flakes.

terengganu.name: Terengganu
terengganu.summary: A sultanate and state on the east coast of Peninsular Malaysia, known by the Arabic honorific 'Abode of Faith' and home to over 1.2 million people, mostly ethnic Malay-Muslims.
